report.executive_summary: Goldman Sachs (GS) experienced a significant financial and strategic divergence between 2023 and 2024, characterized by a strong earnings recovery ($14.28B net income, up 67.64% from $8.52B in 2023) contrasted with deteriorating cash flows and increased regulatory burdens. The firm executed a major strategic retreat from consumer-facing businesses, notably completing the divestiture of GreenSky and Personal Financial Management (PFM) units, while simultaneously expanding its alternatives and capital solutions capabilities. Disclosure quality exhibited a dual trend: while new quantitative metrics and specific risk quantifications (e.g., FICC exposure, tax benefits) were introduced, there was a noticeable reduction in granularity regarding ESG, human capital diversity, and specific governance structures. Regulatory compliance complexities increased with the adoption of T+1 settlement, new SEC climate and data rules, and heightened litigation risks from underwriting activities, despite the resolution of several legacy matters.
report.longitudinal_analysis: Disclosure developments between 2023 and 2024 reveal a shift from prospective uncertainty to realized operational impacts and strategic realignment. In 2023, risks were largely framed as potential headwinds (e.g., SVB liquidity risk, proposed regulations). By 2024, these materialized: T+1 settlement risk moved from prospective to actual operational burden, and the SEC transitioned from proposing to adopting climate and data privacy rules, though some implementations were stayed pending litigation. Strategic disclosure shifted significantly; the 2023 narrative focused on specific transactional exits (GreenSky agreement), whereas 2024 framed these as a broader 'narrowing of consumer focus.' Conversely, transparency declined in non-financial areas, with the removal of specific diversity metrics, climate-human capital linkages, and detailed governance committee structures. Legal disclosures evolved from general contingencies to specific, high-profile litigation escalations (e.g., Rivian, Natera) alongside settlements (Oak Street, Platinum/Palladium). New quantitative disclosures emerged for AI cyber risks, Level 3 liability drivers, and specific capital buffer targets, indicating a move toward more precise risk quantification in certain domains while reducing it in others.
report.financial_analysis: Financial performance improved materially in 2024, with Net Income increasing by $5.76 billion (67.64%) to $14.28 billion and Diluted EPS rising by $17.67 (77.26%) to $40.54. Total Assets grew modestly by 2.09% to $1.68 trillion, while Stockholders' Equity increased by 4.35% to $122.0 billion. Despite earnings growth, cash generation deteriorated; Operating Cash Flow remained negative, worsening from -$12.59 billion in 2023 to -$13.21 billion in 2024, resulting in an Operating Cash Flow to Net Income ratio of -0.93x compared to -1.48x in 2023. Total Debt decreased slightly by 1.72% to $312.3 billion, leading to a reduction in the Debt/Equity ratio from 2.72x in 2023 to 2.56x in 2024. Capital expenditures showed a consistent downward trend, falling 38.21% from 2022 to 2023, and further decreasing by 9.72% in 2024 to $2.09 billion. The improvement in earnings was driven by lower credit loss provisions and resolution of prior impairments, contrasting with the 2023 drag from CRE and consumer divestitures.
limitations: The provided financial metrics only extend through 2024; no data is available for years prior to 2021 or post-2024 to establish a longer-term multi-decade trend.

Segment-specific revenue and earnings data (e.g., FICC, Investment Banking) are referenced in batch findings but specific quantitative values for 2024 segment performance are not provided in the financial_metrics list, limiting granular segment analysis.

While operating cash flow and net income are provided, specific breakdowns of cash flow by investing and financing activities (beyond capital expenditures and debt changes) are limited to batch narrative findings, preventing a full cash flow statement reconciliation analysis.

key_findings.title: Introduction of $300 Billion Credit AUM Growth Target
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces a specific quantitative strategic goal to grow total credit alternative assets to $300 billion by the end of 2028. This represents a formal escalation of the company's strategic priority in alternatives, replacing prior qualitative or surpassed targets with a defined multi-year benchmark for scale and resource allocation.

key_findings.title: Isolation of FICC Guarantee Exposure
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 reporting isolates the company's guarantees for sponsored member clients to the Fixed Income Clearing Corporation (FICC), revealing a maximum payout exposure of $47.44 billion (up from $14.60 billion in 2023). This change separates this high-exposure contingent liability from other securities lending indemnifications, providing clearer visibility into specific operational exposures to clearing corporations.

key_findings.title: T+1 Settlement Risk Materialization
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure shifts the status of the T+1 settlement transition risk from a prospective forward-looking risk in 2023 to an actual current impact in 2024. The 2024 filing states the transition 'has subjected' the company to increased operational risks regarding reporting and timely settlement, indicating the risk has moved from potential to realized in terms of operational burden.

key_findings.title: U.S. Equity Market Structure Regulation Adoption and Stay
key_findings.analysis: Regulatory status changed from proposed rules in 2023 to adopted rules in 2024. Two rules were adopted: one expanding execution quality reporting (effective Dec 2025) and another updating minimum pricing increments. Notably, the SEC stayed the implementation of the pricing increment rule in December 2024 pending litigation, shifting the company's exposure from general proposal risk to active compliance with some parts and legal uncertainty for others.

key_findings.title: Potential Material Tax Benefit from Varian Decision
key_findings.analysis: A new disclosure indicates the company is evaluating a potential material income tax benefit for the 2018 tax year resulting from the U.S. Tax Court's Varian decision on deemed repatriation taxes. While no benefit was recognized as of December 2024, the explicit mention of a potential material impact introduces a new financial opportunity/exposure not disclosed in the prior year.

key_findings.title: Incurring Federal Home Loan Bank Borrowings
key_findings.analysis: The company introduced $5.04 billion in outstanding borrowings from the Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) in 2024, compared to zero in 2023. This represents a significant new source of funding liability and alters the firm's capital resource profile, even as it explicitly states it does not rely on the Federal Reserve discount window.

key_findings.title: Strategic Risk of Narrowing Consumer Focus
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure adds a specific forward-looking warning that future decisions to narrow the focus on consumer-related activities could have a material impact on results of operations. This introduces a specific strategic risk and revenue uncertainty regarding the business model that was not present in the 2023 text.

key_findings.title: Completion of GreenSky Divestiture
key_findings.analysis: The company completed the sale of GreenSky in 2024, transitioning from an agreement to sell disclosed in 2023. This divestiture removed approximately $3.4 billion in assets, including loans, cash, and intangibles, from the balance sheet, fundamentally changing the company's business operations and strategic focus by exiting this platform solution.

key_findings.title: Sea Limited Litigation Settlement in Principle
key_findings.analysis: Regarding the Sea Limited IPO litigation, the status evolved from a court dismissal in 2023 (affirmed in 2023, reversed on appeal in 2024) to a settlement in principle reached in November 2024. Crucially, the settlement does not require a contribution from GS Asia, resolving a significant litigation risk that had been active following the appellate reversal.

key_findings.title: Oak Street Health Litigation Settlement Approval
key_findings.analysis: For the Oak Street Health securities class action, the court approved a settlement in December 2024. The settlement explicitly excludes GS&Co. from contributing to the resolution, thereby eliminating the pending financial liability exposure associated with this litigation that was partially dismissed but still active in 2023.

key_findings.title: Resolution of Platinum and Palladium Manipulation Litigation
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, Goldman Sachs resolved putative class actions regarding the manipulation of platinum and palladium benchmarks. This marks a transition from the 2023 status, where the Second Circuit had reversed a district court dismissal to allow antitrust and Commodity Exchange Act claims to proceed. The 2024 disclosure confirms the court approved a settlement on January 17, 2025, and that the firm has paid its full contribution. This resolves the litigation uncertainty and establishes a concrete financial liability for the firm.

key_findings.title: Finalization of CFPB Investigation with Monetary Penalty
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure shifted from a statement of ongoing cooperation with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) in 2023 to the resolution of the investigation via a consent order in 2024. The 2024 filing specifies that GS Bank USA agreed to a $45 million penalty and approximately $20 million in restitution without admitting or denying findings. The firm has paid the full settlement amount. This quantifies a specific financial loss and regulatory outcome that was previously undefined.

key_findings.title: Disclosure of Level 3 Liability Gains and Drivers
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing introduced new financial data regarding Level 3 other financial liabilities, reporting net realized and unrealized gains of $505 million for the year ended December 2024. This gain was primarily driven by changes in interest rates and foreign exchange impacts on hybrid financial instruments in unsecured long-term borrowings, partially offset by losses in deposits linked to equity price increases. This provides specific performance drivers and P&L attribution that was not explicitly detailed in the prior year's static comparison.

key_findings.title: Completion of Personal Financial Management (PFM) Business Divestiture
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure reported the sale of the Personal Financial Management (PFM) business. The absence of this transaction in the 2024 filing indicates the finalization and completion of this strategic exit. This change reflects the company has exited this line of business, altering its segment composition and strategic focus away from PFM.

key_findings.title: Materialization of Election and Tariff Risks
key_findings.analysis: In 2023, the company disclosed risks associated with upcoming global elections, including the U.S. presidential election, citing potential for market uncertainty and policy changes. By 2024, the disclosure confirmed these elections had occurred and identified specific adverse policy changes, notably the imposition or increase of tariffs, including on imports from China. This shifts the risk profile from hypothetical uncertainty to actual, ongoing regulatory headwinds affecting the business environment.

key_findings.title: Elevation of Generative AI and Infrastructure Cyber Risks
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 cybersecurity disclosures explicitly split broad cyber risks into specific categories, introducing 'Generative AI' and 'bad actors using AI technologies' as distinct threat vectors for fraud, misappropriation, and cyberattacks. This is a material upgrade from 2023, which only generally mentioned AI in the context of cybercriminals. Additionally, the 2024 filing isolated risks related to mobile devices and cloud technologies into a separate disclosure, highlighting the growing reliance on and vulnerability of these infrastructure components.

key_findings.title: Strategic Narrowing of Consumer Business Focus
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduced a new strategic narrative: the company 'narrowed our focus with respect to consumer-related activities' during 2023 and 2024. This is a shift from 2023, which listed specific transactions like the GreenSky sale and GM credit card transition without framing them as part of a broader strategic retreat. The 2024 filing further details the agreement to transition the GM credit card program, expected to complete in 2025, signaling a continued reduction in consumer lending exposure.

key_findings.title: New EU Basel III Cross-Border Banking Restrictions
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing added disclosure regarding new European Union restrictions under Basel III Revisions. These rules restrict the cross-border provision of core banking services (deposit-taking, lending, commitments, and guarantees) into the EU. Consequently, new contracts must be executed out of EU subsidiaries, such as GSBE, with pre-June 2026 contracts grandfathered. This represents a new operational constraint on market access in the EU not present in 2023.

key_findings.title: Adoption of Monthly Portfolio Reporting Requirements
key_findings.analysis: The regulatory landscape for asset management changed significantly in 2024 with the SEC adopting amendments (moving from the 2022/2023 proposal stage) requiring open-end management investment companies to file monthly portfolio reports within 30 days of month-end, replacing the previous 60-day quarterly reporting. The rule also mandates disclosure of liquidity risk service providers. Compliance is required by November 17, 2025, necessitating system enhancements and changes to disclosure controls.

key_findings.title: Finalization of Regulation S-P Cybersecurity Rules
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure marks the transition of Regulation S-P amendments from proposed (2023) to adopted (2024). The final rule requires broker-dealers and investment advisers to adopt incident response policies and notify affected individuals within 30 days of certain cybersecurity incidents. Specific compliance deadlines were established: December 2025 for larger entities and June 2026 for smaller ones. This creates concrete compliance obligations with defined timelines for the firm.

key_findings.title: Increase in Hypothetical Credit Loss Exposure
key_findings.analysis: The hypothetical impact of an adverse economic scenario on the allowance for credit losses increased from $0.7 billion in 2023 to $0.9 billion in 2024, representing a 28.5% rise. This indicates an increased sensitivity to stress conditions in the firm's credit risk profile.

key_findings.title: New Material Risk from Future OECD Tax Guidance
key_findings.analysis: While Pillar II legislation did not materially impact the 2024 effective tax rate, the 2024 disclosure introduces a new forward-looking risk, warning that future OECD guidance in 2025 could result in a material increase to the effective tax rate, contrasting with the 2023 view that the 2024 impact would not be material.

key_findings.title: Formation of Capital Solutions Group
key_findings.analysis: In January 2025, the firm formed the Capital Solutions Group within Global Banking & Markets. This new unit expands the firm's coverage and offerings to financial sponsors and alternative asset management firms, marking a strategic change in business activity.

key_findings.title: Tightening of Regulatory Capital Requirements
key_findings.analysis: The Federal Reserve Board increased the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB) from 5.5% to 6.2% based on the 2024 CCAR submission, raising the Standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement to 13.7% for the period October 1, 2024, through September 30, 2025. This reverses the reduction seen in 2023.

key_findings.title: Divestiture of Seller Financing Loan Portfolio
key_findings.analysis: The firm sold its seller financing loan portfolio, which consisted of loans extended to small- and medium-sized retailers and was included within Platform Solutions. This represents a strategic shift and change in asset composition.

key_findings.title: Significant Increase in Intercompany Secured Loans
key_findings.analysis: Group Inc.'s secured loans to regulated subsidiaries increased substantially from $40.47 billion in 2023 to $59.97 billion in 2024. Additionally, equity investments in subsidiaries such as GS Bank USA increased, reflecting changes in internal capital resource commitments.

key_findings.title: Large Decrease in Cash Reserves in 2024
key_findings.analysis: Cash and cash equivalents decreased by $59.49 billion to $182.09 billion at the end of 2024. This is a significant decline compared to the $248 million decrease reported in 2023, driven primarily by net cash used in investing and operating activities.

key_findings.title: Shift in 2023 Cash Flow Drivers
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 cash flow analysis shows a dramatic reduction in cash outflows compared to 2022. Cash decreased by only $248 million in 2023, compared to a $19.21 billion decrease in 2022. This shift was driven by favorable changes in operating and investing activities and foreign exchange effects.

key_findings.title: 2024 Level 3 Loan Rollforward Results
key_findings.analysis: New data for 2024 reveals net realized and unrealized losses of $8 million on Level 3 loans. This includes $33 million in net realized gains offset by $41 million in net unrealized losses, primarily driven by other principal transactions.

key_findings.title: EMEA Clearing Settlement Election Impact
key_findings.analysis: The firm disclosed a new operational election for an EMEA clearing organization, which would have reduced gross derivative assets by $64.19 billion and liabilities by $62.86 billion as of December 2023. This highlights significant changes in gross exposure and netting efficiency not previously quantified in this manner.

key_findings.title: Adoption of Proportional Amortization for Tax Credit VIEs
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, the firm adopted ASU 2023-02 and elected the proportional amortization method for qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects receiving production tax credits as of January 1, 2024. This new accounting policy election materially changes the financial presentation of these nonconsolidated tax credit VIE investments compared to the prior year.

key_findings.title: Completion of GreenSky Sale Removes Installment Loan Commitments
key_findings.analysis: The firm completed the sale of GreenSky during 2024, resolving the 2023 status where unsecured installment loan commitments of $2.25 billion were held for sale. This transaction removed the associated business line and future lending commitments from the company's operational scope and financial position.

key_findings.title: Issuance of Series X and Y Preferred Stock Alters Capital Structure
key_findings.analysis: The firm issued 90,000 shares of Series X preferred stock in April 2024 and 80,000 shares of Series Y preferred stock in September 2024. These issuances represent a significant change in the company's capital structure and equity profile, introducing new dividend obligations not present in the 2023 disclosures.

key_findings.title: Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock Introduces New Equity Class
key_findings.analysis: In January 2025 (reported in the 2024 filing), the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock. This adds a new class of equity with specific redemption terms starting in 2030 and variable dividend rates thereafter, changing the capital structure and introducing new financial obligations.

key_findings.title: Directional Reversal in Credit Risk-Weighted Assets
key_findings.analysis: Standardized Credit RWAs decreased by $12.15 billion in 2024, a sharp reversal from the $33.71 billion increase in 2023, primarily driven by reduced securities financing transactions. Concurrently, Standardized Market RWAs increased by $7.95 billion in 2024 versus $5.60 billion in 2023. These quantitative shifts materially alter the composition of the company's risk-weighted assets.

key_findings.title: Settlement of Uber IPO Litigation with No Contribution Required
key_findings.analysis: The federal court action regarding the Uber IPO settled on December 4, 2024, with a court approval that did not require a contribution from GS&Co. This resolves the material uncertainty of potential financial liability for this high-profile underwriting matter, shifting the risk status from pending litigation to settled.

key_findings.title: Escalation of Natera Litigation via Class Certification Recommendation
key_findings.analysis: In the Natera IPO litigation, a Magistrate Judge recommended granting class certification in January 2025. This represents a significant escalation from the 2023 status where the motion to dismiss had been partially granted, as class certification materially increases defense costs, potential liability exposure, and settlement likelihood.

key_findings.title: Dismissal of Claims in Olaplex Litigation
key_findings.analysis: The court dismissed all claims against underwriters, including GS&Co, in the Olaplex IPO litigation on February 7, 2025. This materially reduces the company's legal liability and exposure compared to the 2023 status where the case was active and the defendants had moved to dismiss a revised complaint.

key_findings.title: Settlement Approval for Interest Rate Swap Antitrust Litigation
key_findings.analysis: In July 2024, the court preliminarily approved a settlement for the interest rate swap antitrust class action, and the firm paid its contribution into an escrow account. This resolves a major uncertainty from the 2023 period, where the case had moved from a denied class certification to a pending interlocutory appeal, shifting the exposure to a resolved financial obligation.

key_findings.title: De-escalation of Specific Regulatory and Economic Uncertainty Risks
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure explicitly cited general uncertainty regarding economic, political, and regulatory reform as a primary driver negatively impacting client activity. The 2024 filing removes this specific attribution, signaling a meaningful de-escalation or shift in the stated risk profile and primary operational headwinds facing the firm.

key_findings.title: Removal of 2023 Credit Rating Methodology Impact Quantification
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing removes the specific disclosure that a methodology change in Q1 2023 resulted in a $29.6 billion reclassification of loans from non-investment-grade to investment-grade. This removal eliminates visibility into the magnitude of credit quality improvements attributed to internal rating changes, obscuring the historical impact of this specific accounting shift.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Exchange Rule and Foreclosure Legal Risks
key_findings.analysis: New disclosures in 2024 explicitly identify exchange rules requiring market makers to maintain orderly markets as a source of loss and liquidity risk during declining markets. Additionally, new text details specific legal and operational risks associated with foreclosure disputes, including claims of improper foreclosure conduct in volatile markets, which were not previously itemized.

key_findings.title: Update to Strategic Divestiture Examples in Risk Disclosures
key_findings.analysis: The risk disclosure regarding new business initiatives was updated to replace 2023 examples (sale of GreenSky and PFM in Q4 2023) with 2024 events (sale of GreenSky Holdings and transition of the GM credit card program). This shifts the factual basis of the 'write-down' and integration risk narrative to reflect current operational history.

key_findings.title: New FRB Enforcement and Investment Adviser BSA Compliance Risks
key_findings.analysis: Two new regulatory risk disclosures appeared in 2024. First, the firm disclosed the FRB's authority to limit activities or require divestiture of U.S. subsidiaries if an FHC fails capital/management standards. Second, new text highlighted specific 2024 BSA rules requiring investment advisers to implement customer identification and AML/CFT programs by January 1, 2026.

key_findings.title: Material Shift in Operating Expense Drivers
key_findings.analysis: Operating expenses normalized in 2024, decreasing due to the absence of 2023's significant one-time charges ($1.46B CRE impairments, $506M GreenSky write-down, $529M FDIC fee). Conversely, 2024 saw an incremental $71M FDIC fee and a rise in litigation provisions from $115M to $166M, altering the composition of recurring costs.

key_findings.title: Change in Asset & Wealth Management Revenue Drivers
key_findings.analysis: Asset & Wealth Management net revenues grew 16% in 2024 compared to 4% in 2023. The primary growth driver shifted from Management fees and Debt investments (2023) to Equity investments (driven by private equity gains) and Management fees (driven by higher assets under supervision), while Private Banking benefits from the prior year's Marcus loan sale.

key_findings.title: Consolidation of Risk Management Governance Committees
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing merges the 'Firmwide Conduct Committee' and 'Firmwide Operational Risk and Resilience Committee' into a single 'Firmwide Compliance and Operational Risk Committee.' This restructuring combines conduct/compliance oversight with operational risk/resilience oversight and adds the Chief Compliance Officer as a co-chair, altering the firm's risk governance structure.

key_findings.title: Adoption of CFPB Personal Financial Data Rule
key_findings.analysis: The regulatory disclosure evolved from a 2023 proposed CFPB rule to an adopted 2024 rule requiring institutions like GS Bank USA to provide free electronic access to 24 months of transaction data by April 1, 2026. The scope expanded to include credit cards, and obligations were placed on data users like GS&Co.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Fair Value Sensitivity Metrics (Yield and Duration)
key_findings.analysis: In the 2024 filing, the company introduced new quantitative metrics for portfolio risk management, specifically yield (ranging 3.8% to 12.3%, weighted average 8.9%) and duration (ranging 2.0 to 5.4 years, weighted average 2.9 years) as of December 2024. This represents a material change in disclosure transparency regarding interest rate risk exposure that was not present in the 2023 filing.

key_findings.title: Reduction in Property and Equipment Impairments
key_findings.analysis: The company reported recognized impairments of $228 million in 2024, a significant decrease from the $1.578 billion recognized in 2023 (comprising $1.46 billion for commercial real estate in CIEs and $118 million for capitalized software). This decline indicates a stabilization in asset values for these specific segments compared to the previous year's peak.

key_findings.title: Quantification of Proportional Amortization Investments
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure provides specific quantification of investments using the proportional amortization method, totaling $2.15 billion as of December 2024. This includes $2.15 billion in accrued unfunded commitments expected to be funded by year-end 2026, primarily in qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects. This detailed aggregation offers new visibility into tax credit VIE exposure.

key_findings.title: Reversal in Advanced Credit Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) Trend
key_findings.analysis: Advanced Credit RWAs shifted direction, increasing by $3.14 billion in 2024 compared to a $13.44 billion decrease in 2023. The 2024 increase was driven primarily by higher lending exposures (commitments, guarantees, loans) and counterparty credit risk, whereas the prior year's decrease was driven by reduced counterparty risk. This signals a material change in the firm's credit risk profile and capital resource utilization.

key_findings.title: Disclosure of Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) and Performance Metrics
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing explicitly identifies the President and COO as the CODM and details the specific metrics used for resource allocation and performance assessment, including total net revenues, pre-tax earnings, and return on average common equity. This information was absent in the 2023 segment disclosures, providing new insight into internal management priorities and decision-making processes.

key_findings.title: Litigation Progression in DiDi Underwriting Action
key_findings.analysis: In the DiDi securities class action, the court denied the defendants' motions to dismiss in March 2024, and plaintiffs moved for class certification in January 2025. This marks a significant escalation in legal risk and potential liability compared to 2023, when motions to dismiss were still pending.

key_findings.title: Class Certification Granted in Rivian IPO Litigation
key_findings.analysis: The court granted class certification in the federal Rivian IPO class action in July 2024. This is a critical milestone that materially increases the potential for settlement or judgment liability and defense costs compared to 2023, where only a motion for class certification had been filed.

key_findings.title: Ninth Circuit Appeal Initiated in Robinhood IPO Litigation
key_findings.analysis: Although the district court dismissed the Robinhood IPO complaint without leave to amend in January 2024, plaintiffs appealed to the Ninth Circuit in February 2024. This appeal reactivates the litigation risk and creates appellate exposure, changing the legal posture from a dismissed case to an active appeal.

key_findings.title: Ninth Circuit Appeal Initiated in ON24 IPO Litigation
key_findings.analysis: Following the dismissal with prejudice of the ON24 IPO complaint in March 2024, plaintiffs appealed to the Ninth Circuit in April 2024. Similar to the Robinhood matter, this appeal introduces continued legal uncertainty and potential liability despite the favorable trial-level ruling.

key_findings.title: Stay of Proceedings in VRDO Antitrust Litigation
key_findings.analysis: Proceedings in the VRDO antitrust class action were stayed in February 2024 pending interlocutory appeal of the class certification to the Second Circuit. While this delays immediate resolution, the grant of review by the appellate court signifies a material development that could ultimately determine the viability of the class action and the associated financial exposure.

key_findings.title: Removal of SVB-Specific Liquidity Risk Example
key_findings.analysis: In 2023, Goldman Sachs explicitly cited the Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) collapse and social media-driven deposit flight as a specific risk to its liquidity position. This example is absent in the 2024 filing. This change suggests the company no longer views this acute, event-driven risk as a primary exposure, indicating a stabilization in its perceived liquidity risk landscape following the 2023 banking sector events.

key_findings.title: Reduction in Disclosed Credit Rating Downside Exposure
key_findings.analysis: The estimated collateral requirements in the event of a credit rating downgrade changed materially between 2023 and 2024. The one-notch downgrade exposure increased from $271 million to $315 million, while the two-notch downgrade exposure decreased significantly from $1.58 billion to $1.20 billion. This indicates a shift in the company's specific financial sensitivity to credit actions, potentially reflecting changes in derivative liabilities or collateral agreements.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Political Uncertainty in Regulatory Risks
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure explicitly introduces 'Recent political developments' as a source of uncertainty regarding new laws, regulations, and enforcement interpretations. This specific attribution was not present in the 2023 generic references to legal changes, signaling a heightened perception of regulatory unpredictability driven by the political environment.

key_findings.title: Separation of US and EU Climate Regulatory Risks
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing splits the previous general climate regulatory disclosure into distinct US and EU components. It highlights specific US regulatory actions (such as the FRB pilot and NYDFS guidance) and distinct EU requirements (CSRD, CSDDD), including due diligence obligations. This separation marks an expansion in the detail of regulatory exposure, particularly regarding conflicting jurisdictional expectations and specific compliance burdens.

key_findings.title: Removal of Specific Risk Governance Structures
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 filing explicitly disclosed the 'Firmwide Risk Council' (co-chaired by CFO and CRO) and the 'Firmwide Capital Committee' (co-chaired by Head of Credit Risk and co-head of Global Financing Group). These specific governance bodies and their leadership compositions are removed from the 2024 disclosure, representing a meaningful reduction in the transparency of the internal risk and capital governance structure.

key_findings.title: Addition of Registered Security-Based Swap Dealer Entities
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure adds two entities, GSI and GSFM, to the list of subsidiaries registered as security-based swap dealers with the SEC, expanding from the previous list which only included GS&Co., GS Bank USA, and GSBE. This change broadens the scope of the company's entities subject to specific SEC regulations regarding capital, margin, and reporting.

key_findings.title: New Human Capital and Compliance Disclosures
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing introduces several new data points and compliance obligations not present in 2023. These include quantitative metrics on workforce stability (average Management Committee tenure of 24 years, all employees 6 years, and >40% campus hires) and the implementation of the Corporate Transparency Act (CTA), which requires beneficial ownership reporting starting in 2024/2025.

key_findings.title: Transition from Historical Credit Methodology Change to Current Operations
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure detailed a specific historical event: a $2.78 billion reclassification of commercial lending commitments due to a change in internal credit rating methodology in 2023. This specific retrospective disclosure is absent in 2024, reflecting a transition from reporting structural accounting/risk changes to focusing on current operational volumes.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Stayed SEC Climate Disclosure Rules
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces the SEC's final climate disclosure rules, noting they are currently stayed pending litigation. This is a new regulatory development in 2024 not present in the 2023 disclosures, which only covered federal bank regulatory principles and SEC Names Rule amendments. This adds a layer of regulatory uncertainty and litigation risk to the company's ESG compliance landscape.

key_findings.title: Executive Leadership Changes in Risk and Treasury Roles
key_findings.analysis: Between the 2023 and 2024 filings, the Chief Risk Officer role changed from Mr. Lee to Mr. Golten (effective January 2025), and the Global Treasurer role changed from Mr. Berlinski to Ms. Halio (effective May 2024). These are key financial control positions, representing a meaningful shift in the organization's risk management and capital structure leadership.

key_findings.title: Goodwill Impairment Charges Linked to Divestitures
key_findings.analysis: The company recorded specific goodwill impairment charges due to divestiture activities: $504 million for Consumer platforms in Q2 2023 (GreenSky sale exploration) and $14 million for Transaction banking in Q3 2024 (seller financing loan portfolio sale). These discrete losses materially impact the composition of goodwill and reported earnings for those respective periods.

key_findings.title: Shift in Revenue Drivers in Other Principal Transactions
key_findings.analysis: Other principal transactions revenues increased 119% to $4.65 billion in 2024, up from $2.13 billion in 2023. The primary drivers shifted from borrowing-related derivatives in 2023 to private equity investments, funding-related derivatives, and the impact of the Marcus loan portfolio sale in 2024. This indicates a significant change in the sources of trading profits and investment strategy.

key_findings.title: Update to Forward-Looking Effective Tax Rate
key_findings.analysis: The company updated its forward-looking effective tax rate estimate from 22% for 2024 to 21% for 2025. This 1 percentage point decrease reflects a shift in the company's tax outlook, potentially due to Pillar II impacts or other strategic tax planning, which is a key financial metric for investor modeling.

key_findings.title: Drastic Reduction in Credit Loss Provisions
key_findings.analysis: Provision for credit losses decreased significantly from $401 million in 2023 to $40 million in 2024. The 2023 provisions were primarily driven by the commercial real estate portfolio, whereas the 2024 reduction suggests the resolution or stabilization of those specific credit risks, materially improving the segment's cost structure.

key_findings.title: Change in Primary Market Driver for Asset Growth
key_findings.analysis: In the Asset & Wealth Management segment, the primary driver of assets under supervision shifted from bond prices in 2023 to global equity prices in 2024. This change in market performance drivers alters the risk profile and revenue generation dynamics for the segment, particularly regarding fee compression and asset withdrawal risks.

key_findings.title: Substantial Improvement in Asset & Wealth Management Earnings
key_findings.analysis: Asset & Wealth Management experienced a dramatic improvement in 2024, with pre-tax earnings tripling from $1.36 billion to $4.55 billion and operating expenses decreasing 9%. This turnaround was driven by lower commercial real estate impairments in Closed-Ended Investments (CIEs) and higher compensation linked to improved performance, marking a fundamental change in the segment's profitability.

key_findings.title: Strategic Retrenchment in Consumer-Related Activities
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure replaces specific financial impairment figures for Consumer platforms (which totaled ~$1 billion in 2023) and transaction banking metrics with cross-references to a 'Narrowing our Focus on Consumer-Related Activities' section. This change in disclosure substance signals a strategic shift away from consumer-related business lines, prioritizing strategic narrative over historical financial performance details for this segment.

key_findings.title: Shift in Primary Drivers of Asset Growth Composition
key_findings.analysis: Between 2023 and 2024, Goldman Sachs experienced a meaningful shift in its balance sheet structure. While total assets grew in both years ($199.80 billion in 2023 vs. $34.38 billion in 2024), the composition of growth changed significantly. In 2023, growth was driven by trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements. In 2024, growth was driven by trading assets, investments, and loans, with significant decreases in cash and collateralized agreements. This indicates a transition away from collateralized agreement growth towards loan expansion and reduced cash holdings.

key_findings.title: Update to Annual Attributed Equity Adjustments Across Business Segments
key_findings.analysis: The company updated its attributed equity allocations for its business segments. For the adjustment effective January 1, 2024, Platform Solutions saw an increase of $1.6 billion, while Asset & Wealth Management and Global Banking & Markets saw decreases of $1.2 billion and $0.4 billion, respectively. The 2024 disclosure further provided the adjustments for January 1, 2025, where Global Banking & Markets increased by $0.4 billion, while Asset & Wealth Management and Platform Solutions decreased by $0.3 billion and $0.1 billion, respectively. This reflects the annual review process based on stress test results and regulatory capital requirements.

key_findings.title: Disclosure of Increased Future G-SIB Surcharge Rate
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces a specific quantitative update regarding the Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB) surcharge. While the 2023 disclosure noted a 3.0% surcharge for 2023 and 2024, the 2024 disclosure explicitly states the surcharge is expected to rise to 3.5% beginning in 2026. This introduces a new, forward-looking regulatory capital obligation not present in the prior year's static disclosure.

key_findings.title: Removal of GreenSky Financing and Addition of Transaction Banking Services
key_findings.analysis: The scope of the Platform Solutions segment has changed significantly. The 2023 disclosure highlighted point-of-sale financing through GreenSky. In 2024, GreenSky is no longer mentioned; instead, the disclosure emphasizes the provision of transaction banking, deposit-taking, payment solutions, and cash management services for corporate and institutional clients. This indicates a strategic pivot away from consumer point-of-sale financing toward commercial banking services.

key_findings.title: Quantification of Investment Losses and Commercial Real Estate Risk
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure provides specific quantitative results for Level 3 investments in 2023, which were not explicitly detailed in the provided 2023 evidence. It reports net realized and unrealized losses of $259 million, driven by $463 million in net realized gains offset by $722 million in net unrealized losses. The disclosure attributes these unrealized losses primarily to equity securities and securities backed by real estate due to ongoing weakness in the commercial real estate market.

key_findings.title: Addition of Floating-Rate Asset Cash Flow Hedge Scope
key_findings.analysis: The firm expanded its hedging activities to explicitly include managing the exposure to the variability of forecasted cash flows associated with certain floating-rate assets. While the 2023 disclosure listed hedges for fixed-rate borrowings, foreign exchange risk, and net investments, the 2024 disclosure adds floating-rate asset cash flow variability. This change was operationalized in Q4 2024 by designating interest rate swaps as cash flow hedges.

key_findings.title: Shift to Fair Value Accounting for Non-USD Short-Term Financings
key_findings.analysis: There was a significant change in the accounting treatment for non-U.S. dollar-denominated short-term other secured financings. In 2023, these were held at amortized cost with a reported weighted average interest rate of 0.47%. In 2024, all such financings were held at fair value under the fair value option, and no interest rate was reported for 2024. This shift from amortized cost to fair value alters the measurement basis and risk exposure disclosure for this liability class.

key_findings.title: Change in Specific Divestiture-Driven Impairment Events
key_findings.analysis: The nature of goodwill impairments changed between years. In 2023, the firm recorded a $504 million impairment charge for Consumer platforms linked to the potential sale of GreenSky. In 2024, the firm recorded a $14 million impairment for 'Transaction banking and other' triggered by the planned sale of the seller financing loan portfolio. The shift reflects different business units and significantly different financial magnitudes.

key_findings.title: Significant Increase in Affordable Housing and Renewable Energy Investments
key_findings.analysis: The firm's capital allocation in qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects saw substantial growth. Funded investments increased from $1.13 billion in December 2023 to $3.46 billion in December 2024. Additionally, the scope of these investments expanded to explicitly include renewable energy projects alongside affordable housing, representing a significant increase in capital exposure to these sectors.

key_findings.title: Strategic Exit from Unsecured Installment Lending
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, GS ceased providing unsecured installment loan commitments in the third quarter, marking a strategic exit from this specific consumer lending product line that was active in 2023. This change alters the company's business activities and risk exposure profile compared to the prior year, where such commitments were explicitly listed alongside credit card lines.

key_findings.title: New Risk Characterization for Derivatives
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces a specific assertion that the carrying value of derivatives is considered the best indication of payment or performance risk for individual contracts. This new perspective on risk measurement was not present in the 2023 disclosure and may influence how investors interpret the risk exposure of the firm's derivative portfolio.

key_findings.title: Shift in Capital Ratio Drivers Including Market RWA Decrease
key_findings.analysis: The drivers for the increase in GS Bank USA's risk-based capital ratios shifted in 2024. While 2023 increases were driven principally by net earnings partially offset by increased Credit RWAs, 2024 improvements reflected net earnings, decreased Market RWAs, and an increase in Credit RWAs. The inclusion of decreased Market RWAs as a primary contributor represents a meaningful change in capital resource dynamics.

key_findings.title: Increase in Regulated Subsidiary Capital Requirements
key_findings.analysis: The minimum equity capital required to be maintained in regulated subsidiaries increased from $95.80 billion in 2023 to $98.48 billion in 2024, against a total equity investment rise from $133.75 billion to $140.79 billion. This reflects an increase in the scale of capital locked in regulated entities to satisfy regulatory and internal policy requirements.

key_findings.title: Granular Disclosure of State and Local Tax Assets
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing introduces specific details regarding $7 million in deferred tax assets and a $1 million valuation allowance for state and local capital loss carryforwards. This level of granularity regarding specific asset classes represents a material change in the depth of tax asset disclosure compared to the broader 2023 reporting.

key_findings.title: Disclosure of SVBFG Governmental Investigation Cooperation
key_findings.analysis: GS introduced a new disclosure in 2024 stating it is cooperating with governmental investigations into SVBFG, specifically citing SVB's March 2023 engagement of the firm for a capital raise and securities portfolio sale. This signals a new compliance condition and potential exposure to regulatory scrutiny not previously disclosed in this context.

key_findings.title: New Underwriting Litigation Risks Disclosed
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure adds significant legal risks by detailing specific securities class action litigations related to the IPOs of Bright Health, Yatsen, and Rent the Runway. Notably, the Bright Health complaint was dismissed but appealed, Yatsen's was dismissed, and Rent the Runway's was partially dismissed, representing a change in the breadth and specificity of disclosed underwriting litigation risks compared to 2023.

key_findings.title: Significant Escalation in Legal Proceedings: New Underwriting Litigation and Reversal of Prior Dismissals
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces three new securities class action lawsuits involving GS&Co. as an underwriter, representing new legal and reputational risks not present in 2023: (1) Opendoor Technologies, where the court vacated dismissal of certain claims in May 2024 (gs_2023_2024_M1274); (2) Silvergate Capital, which adds a Layer 11 bankruptcy risk from September 2024 to the existing litigation (gs_2023_2024_M1276); and (3) agilon health, a consolidated class action filed in March 2024 (gs_2023_2024_M1279). Additionally, the firm faced a major setback in the odd-lot corporate bond antitrust litigation, where the Second Circuit vacated a previous district court dismissal in July 2024, reversing a favorable 2023 outcome and exposing the firm to continued liability (gs_2023_2024_M1284).

key_findings.title: Reduced Transparency in ESG, Human Capital, and Governance Disclosures
key_findings.analysis: GS significantly narrowed its disclosure scope across non-financial risk factors in 2024 compared to 2023. The firm removed specific links between climate change perceptions and employee recruitment/retention risks (gs_2023_2024_M0004). It also ceased reporting specific diversity metrics for partnership and managing director classes (gs_2023_2024_M0007), as well as specific quantitative hiring goals and results for analysts and associates (gs_2023_2024_M0008). Furthermore, detailed descriptions of the 'Firmwide Commitments Committee,' including its co-chair composition and oversight role in equity underwriting, were removed from the governance section (gs_2023_2024_M0053).

key_findings.title: Removal of Operational, Regulatory, and Segment-Specific Financial Detail
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing omits material operational and regulatory details previously disclosed in 2023. Specifically, the disclosure regarding the SEC's private fund adviser reform rules—including the requirement for system enhancements and compliance deadlines through March 2025—was removed (gs_2023_2024_M0017). In financial reporting, the firm removed the detailed variance analysis for FICC net revenues, including the specific $12.06 billion figure, the 18% decrease, and the causal drivers such as lower client activity and currency/commodities performance (gs_2023_2024_M0044). This reduces the granularity available to investors regarding asset management compliance burdens and fixed income market dynamics.

key_findings.title: Reduction in transparency regarding suitability oversight governance
key_findings.analysis: In the 2023 filing, Goldman Sachs disclosed specific governance details for the Firmwide Suitability Committee, including its mandate to set product and transaction suitability standards, its role in ensuring regional consistency, and its co-chair composition (CCO and advisory director). These specific details were removed in the 2024 disclosure. This reduction in granularity may obscure the firm's internal controls and reporting lines for suitability oversight, making it harder for investors to assess the robustness of these governance structures.

key_findings.title: Disappearance of specific credit rating methodology change disclosures
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosures explicitly documented two significant one-time changes to credit assessment methodologies: a Q1 2023 change to consider collateral in internal ratings for collateralized loans, and a Q4 2023 switch from internal ratings to FICO/LTV metrics for U.S. residential mortgages, which resulted in a quantified reclassification impact of $2.5-$5.4 billion. These specific transition narratives and their quantified impacts are absent in the 2024 filing. While the new methodologies may still be in use, the removal of the disclosure regarding the *change event* and its historical financial impact reduces visibility into recent adjustments to risk assessment models and their material effect on prior period loan classifications.

key_findings.title: Confirmation of material operational impact from market volatility
key_findings.analysis: While 2023 described the theoretical risks of market volatility (increased risk, inventory reduction, forced losses), the 2024 disclosure adds a concrete, quantified example: in August 2024, significant market volatility adversely affected activity levels, increased market Risk-Weighted Assets (RWAs), and negatively impacted results on specific days. This moves the disclosure from abstract risk description to evidence of recent, tangible adverse operational and capital metric impacts.

key_findings.title: Introduction of new regulatory compliance risks regarding cybersecurity audits
key_findings.analysis: A new disclosure in 2024 highlights a 2024 proposal by the California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) under the CCPA for cybersecurity audits, risk assessments, and automated decision-making technology regulations. This represents a new, specific regulatory development expanding the compliance landscape beyond general privacy laws, potentially imposing new substantive requirements on the firm's security operations.

key_findings.title: Significant growth in earnings and cost structure shift
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure reports an 11% increase in operating expenses ($19.98 billion) and a substantial 29% increase in pre-tax earnings ($14.92 billion) compared to 2023. The expense growth is explicitly attributed to higher transaction-based costs and compensation, indicating a change in the operational cost driver structure alongside strong profitability improvements.

key_findings.title: Shift in credit loss provision drivers from one-time portfolio sale to paydowns
key_findings.analysis: The net benefit from the provision for credit losses decreased significantly from $508 million in 2023 to $232 million in 2024. The underlying driver shifted from a one-time reserve reduction related to the sale of the Marcus loans portfolio in 2023 to paydowns in the wholesale portfolio in 2024. This indicates a change in the nature and sustainability of the credit benefits realized.

key_findings.title: Enhanced granularity in deposit composition and insurance status
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing introduces detailed disclosures on the composition of deposits, breaking them down into savings/demand, time, consumer (Marcus/Apple Card), sweep, transaction banking, and institutional categories. It also explicitly quantifies FDIC-insured deposits ($234.54 billion) and non-U.S. insured deposits ($25.98 billion). This new granular data provides investors with clearer visibility into the stability and regulatory protection of the firm's core funding sources.

key_findings.title: Increased capital returns and new buffer target declaration
key_findings.analysis: Capital returned to shareholders increased from $9.39 billion in 2023 to $11.80 billion in 2024. Furthermore, the 2024 disclosure introduces a specific policy target of maintaining a '50 to 100 basis point buffer above our capital requirement,' a specific metric not present in the 2023 disclosure. This clarifies the firm's capital management philosophy and forward-looking stance on capital adequacy.

key_findings.title: Permanent increase in risk appetite limits
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, Goldman Sachs implemented a permanent increase to its firmwide Value-at-Risk (VaR) risk limit, citing higher volatility and increased exposures. This contrasts with 2023, where no permanent changes were made, though temporary adjustments occurred. This permanent shift signals an expansion in the firm's risk appetite and capacity to take on market risk, potentially affecting future risk profiles.

key_findings.title: Expansion of Hedge Accounting Scope to Floating-Rate Assets
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, Goldman Sachs added a new application of hedge accounting by using interest rate swaps to manage the variability of forecasted cash flows associated with certain floating-rate assets. This represents an expansion of the firm's risk management strategy beyond the fixed-rate borrowings, CDs, and securities managed via hedge accounting in 2023, indicating a shift or increase in exposure to floating-rate assets.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Cash Flow Hedge Accounting Policy
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces specific accounting treatments for new Cash Flow Hedges, noting that gains or losses are included in other comprehensive income (OCI) and reclassified to interest income/expense when hedged cash flows impact earnings. This policy was not disclosed in 2023, completing the accounting disclosure for the expanded hedging activities identified in the same period.

key_findings.title: Significant Increase in Fair Value Option Usage for Secured Financings
key_findings.analysis: The quantification of the fair value option election shows a material increase in the carrying amount of other secured financings accounted for at fair value, rising from $12.55 billion in 2023 to $27.99 billion in 2024. Additionally, the 2024 disclosure specifies that all U.S. dollar-denominated short-term and non-U.S. dollar-denominated long-term other secured financings were held at fair value, providing greater transparency into the composition and magnitude of earnings volatility mitigation strategies.

key_findings.title: Reclassification and Reduced Exposure of Investment Fund VIEs
key_findings.analysis: Beginning in Q4 2024, investment fund Variable Interest Entities (VIEs) were reclassified into 'tax credit and other investing.' The carrying value of the firm's variable interests in these specific VIEs decreased substantially from $91 million in 2023 to $9 million in 2024, altering the financial presentation and reducing the disclosed risk exposure associated with these entities.

key_findings.title: Increase in Quarterly Common Stock Dividend
key_findings.analysis: The Board of Directors increased the quarterly common stock dividend from $2.75 per share in early 2024 to $3.00 per share in early 2025. This quantitative increase signals improved financial capacity and serves as a positive indicator of management's confidence in the firm's earnings stability and cash flow generation.

key_findings.title: Updated Net Operating Loss (NOL) Carryforward Expiration Timeline
key_findings.analysis: The firm updated the expiration timeline for its U.S. federal, state, local, and foreign NOL carryforwards from 2024 (in 2023 disclosures) to 2025 (in 2024 disclosures). This shift suggests the firm has utilized or extended the life of these tax assets, reducing the near-term risk of expiration while maintaining that any expiration would not have a material impact on operations. Deferred tax assets related to NOLs decreased from $929 million to $786 million.

key_findings.title: Resolution of DOJ Deferred Prosecution Agreement (1MDB)
key_findings.analysis: A significant legal contingency was resolved with the dismissal of the conspiracy charge against the firm under the Deferred Prosecution Agreement (DPA) with the DOJ on May 6, 2024. This dismissal effectively closed the three-year DPA term, removing associated compliance monitoring obligations and legal uncertainty that existed during the 2023 reporting period.

key_findings.title: Dismissal of ContextLogic IPO Litigation Complaint
key_findings.analysis: The court dismissed the third consolidated amended complaint in the ContextLogic IPO securities class action without leave to amend in August 2024. This favorable legal development significantly de-escalated the risk of adverse judgment in this specific matter compared to the prior year, although a subsequent motion to alter judgment was filed.

key_findings.title: Dismissal of MINISO IPO Litigation Complaint (With Leave to Amend)
key_findings.analysis: The court granted the motion to dismiss the second amended complaint in the MINISO IPO securities class action on February 23, 2024. While this represents a procedural victory reducing immediate exposure, the grant of leave to amend means the litigation is not fully resolved, keeping it a material ongoing contingency.

key_findings.title: Dismissal of FIGS IPO Litigation Claims Against Underwriters
key_findings.analysis: In the FIGS IPO securities class action, the court dismissed all claims against underwriter defendants, including Goldman Sachs, on January 10, 2025. Although plaintiffs appealed this decision in February 2025, the dismissal of claims against the underwriters marks a significant favorable development in the litigation status compared to the unresolved or pending nature of such claims in prior periods.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Continued Legal Uncertainty in CDS Antitrust Litigation
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, the company disclosed that plaintiffs appealed the January 2024 court order enforcing a 2015 settlement and release in the Credit Default Swap antitrust class action. While the 2023 filing noted the enforcement and stay, the 2024 update adds the fact that the appeal to the Second Circuit introduces continued uncertainty and potential reversal of the injunction, indicating the legal exposure was not fully resolved as of year-end 2024.

key_findings.title: Materialization of Historical Risk Management Failures
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure represents a substantive shift in risk narrative by changing the language from a forward-looking hypothesis ('may incur losses') in 2023 to an admission of past actualization ('have in the past incurred... losses') in 2024. This confirms that ineffective risk management processes resulted in realized financial losses, moving the risk from theoretical to historical fact.

key_findings.title: Emergence of T+1 Settlement Operational Risk
key_findings.analysis: A new specific risk factor was added in 2024 regarding the U.S. transition to a T+1 settlement timeframe. This introduces a distinct operational compliance risk and potential for fines/penalties associated with this regulatory change in 2024, which was not present or specified in the 2023 risk disclosures.

key_findings.title: Resolution of Multiple Underwriting Litigation Matters
key_findings.analysis: Several legal proceedings disclosed in 2023 were resolved in 2024, leading to their removal from the risk/legal disclosures. Specifically, the GoHealth IPO litigation concluded with a preliminary settlement requiring no contribution from Goldman Sachs; the Waterdrop IPO litigation saw the dismissal affirmed by the Second Circuit; and the Reata Pharmaceuticals litigation concluded with a preliminary settlement requiring no contribution from Goldman Sachs. These changes indicate a reduction in specific contingent liabilities and legal uncertainty for these matters.

key_findings.title: Change in Goodwill Impairment Status
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure highlighted a decrease in goodwill primarily due to impairment associated with Consumer platforms. The 2024 disclosure indicates no such impairment was recognized, marking a material change in the financial assessment of reporting units and asset values for the year 2024.

key_findings.title: Removal of Segment Revenue and Risk Disclosures
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing removes specific quantitative performance metrics for Global Banking & Markets (including the $30 billion revenue figure and -8% variance) and specific risk disclosures regarding ownership in public services (airports, toll roads) and physical commodities infrastructure. This suggests a change in disclosure policy or business composition, eliminating detailed analysis of specific revenue drivers and niche asset risk exposures previously highlighted.

key_findings.title: Escalation of AI-driven competitive threat
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure explicitly asserts that competitors are using AI to gain specific cost and productivity advantages, moving beyond the 2023 general risk of market share loss to a concrete competitive disadvantage. This highlights a material shift in the nature of technology-related competitive pressure.

key_findings.title: Strategic segmentation of Global Banking & Markets
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing splits the description of Global Banking & Markets into two distinct disclosures: one focusing on revenue sources and the other on client serving activities. This separation provides a clearer, more granular definition of the segment's financial mechanics and service offerings.

key_findings.title: Growth in Community TeamWorks initiative
key_findings.analysis: Volunteering metrics increased significantly in 2024, with hours rising from 94,000 to 103,000 and participants from 18,000 to 19,000. The disclosure also explicitly states that volunteering 'strengthens employee bonds with the firm,' adding a specific cultural value assertion not present in the prior year.

key_findings.title: Omission of FCA regulation for GSBE London branch
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure omits the specific sentence regarding the FCA regulation of GSBE's London branch, which was present in the 2023 text. This represents a change in the disclosed regulatory jurisdiction details for a significant entity.

key_findings.title: Expanded risk retention scope and EU/UK regulatory details
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure expands the scope of subsidiaries subject to risk retention requirements to include GSIB and clarifies the specific nature of EU/UK regulations (due diligence, monitoring). This narrows and quantifies the compliance exposure compared to the broader 2023 statement.

key_findings.title: Introduction of regulatory uncertainty for ESG directives
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces significant uncertainty regarding the transposition and potential revision of EU directives (CSRD, CSDDD), explicitly mentioning the 'Omnibus package.' This qualitative escalation from 'subject to requirements' to 'uncertainty around timing and scope' materially changes the compliance risk profile.

key_findings.title: Recovery in investment banking volume and mixed market activity
key_findings.analysis: While 2023 described a broadly negative impact on investment banking and market-making, 2024 discloses increased underwriting volumes (debt and equity) and mixed market-making activity. This indicates a recovery and divergence in revenue drivers compared to the previous year's subdued activity.

key_findings.title: Significant increase in debt underwriting volumes
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure notes that debt underwriting volumes 'increased significantly' compared with the prior year, contrasting with the previous year's decline or stagnation. This change in industry volume trends is a meaningful shift in the operational environment.

key_findings.title: Narrowing of wealth advisory target and introduction of Marcus
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure narrows the scope of 'tailored wealth advisory' to 'ultra-high-net-worth' clients, whereas the 2023 disclosure described services for the 'wealth spectrum'. Additionally, it explicitly introduces 'Marcus' consumer deposits as a source of deposits.

key_findings.title: Shift in magnitude and mix of liability growth drivers
key_findings.analysis: Total liabilities increased by $29.29 billion in 2024 compared to $200.08 billion in 2023. The change in magnitude and specific mix of liability funding sources (driven primarily by collateralized financings and deposits in 2024 vs. multiple drivers in 2023) represents a meaningful change in the firm's financial position.

key_findings.title: Expansion of Risk Oversight Mandate to Include Strategic Initiatives
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, the Firmwide New Activity Committee's mandate was explicitly expanded to include 'significant strategic business initiatives,' referred by the Firmwide Enterprise Risk Committee. Previously, in 2023, the committee's scope was limited to new activities and reassessing previously approved significant activities for changes in complexity or reputation. This change broadens the oversight structure, subjecting strategic business initiatives to the same risk scrutiny as new activities.

key_findings.title: Reversal in Credit Exposure and Counterparty Quality Trends
key_findings.analysis: The company's credit risk profile underwent a meaningful shift between 2023 and 2024. In 2023, aggregate credit exposure increased compared to 2022, while the percentage of non-investment-grade exposure decreased. In contrast, 2024 disclosures show aggregate credit exposure decreased compared to 2023 (driven by lower central bank deposits), while the percentage of non-investment-grade exposure increased (due to a decrease in investment-grade exposure related to those deposits).

key_findings.title: New Explicit Definition and Strategic Role of Reputational Risk
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces a specific definition of reputational risk as negative publicity causing customer base decline, litigation, or revenue reductions, and explicitly links reputation to the firm's evaluation of business opportunities based on ethics, suitability, and transparency. This was a new disclosure in 2024, not present in the 2023 text which mentioned the committee but lacked this specific impact linkage and policy criterion.

key_findings.title: Significant Increase in Collateralized Borrowing Volume
key_findings.analysis: The amount of other secured financings collateralized by trading assets, investments, and loans nearly tripled, rising from $8.38 billion in December 2023 to $24.39 billion in December 2024. This substantial increase alters the firm's leverage profile and collateral usage, despite a concurrent decrease in nonrecourse secured financings.

key_findings.title: Shift in Corporate Loan Portfolio Industry Concentration
key_findings.analysis: The composition of the top five industry concentrations for corporate loans changed in 2024. 'Consumer & retail' (11% in 2023) was replaced by 'financial institutions' (9% in 2024) in the top five list, indicating a shift in strategic lending focus or market exposure within the corporate loan book.

key_findings.title: Addition of Year-End Unencumbered Asset Metrics
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure added specific year-end (Q4) fair value averages for 'Other Unencumbered Assets' ($295.49 billion in Q4 2024 vs $286.51 billion in Q4 2023), whereas the 2023 disclosure only provided annual and three-month averages. This provides more granular data on the liquidity buffer composition, though the qualitative assessment that these assets are not liquid enough for GCLA inclusion remained unchanged.

key_findings.title: Change in Fair Value Level 3 Transfer Drivers
key_findings.analysis: The drivers for transfers into Level 3 liabilities changed between the two periods. In 2024, transfers were due to reduced transparency of 'credit spreads and volatility inputs' for unsecured borrowings, whereas in 2023, transfers involved 'volatility and correlation inputs'. This indicates a shift in the market conditions and valuation inputs affecting the transparency of specific instruments.

key_findings.title: Increase in Assets Held for Sale in Asset & Wealth Management
key_findings.analysis: Assets held for sale related to consolidated investments within Asset & Wealth Management increased significantly from $327 million in December 2023 to $517 million in December 2024. This nearly 60% increase represents a meaningful change in the composition and liquidity posture of the firm's balance sheet, primarily consisting of property and equipment.

key_findings.title: Refinement of Unsecured Borrowing Disclosure
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, the disclosure for unsecured long-term borrowings introduced specific narrative details regarding their composition, stating they consist 'principally of senior borrowings with maturities through 2061,' and provided a distinct fair value of $89.19 billion for this category. This represents a shift from the 2023 disclosure, which only reported aggregate carrying and fair values ($155.47 billion carrying, $157.75 billion fair value) without specifying the senior/subordinated mix or separating fair-value-option borrowings.

key_findings.title: Entry into GreenSky Seller Financing
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure marks a significant expansion of the firm's seller financing activities by introducing $2.12 billion in financing for GreenSky loan sales, a new counterparty not mentioned in 2023. This contrasts with the 2023 disclosure, which exclusively cited seller financing for Marcus loans ($2.7 billion in 2023), indicating a diversification in the firm's operational footprint and credit exposure within its lending channels.

key_findings.title: Expansion of VIE Activities to Tax Credits
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure explicitly adds investments in VIEs focused on 'qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects' to generate returns via tax credits. This is a new category compared to the 2023 disclosure, which described VIE activities limited to real estate, performing/nonperforming debt, distressed assets, and power-related assets, signaling an expansion into tax credit investing strategies.

key_findings.title: Regulatory Capital Evolution as Repurchase Driver
key_findings.analysis: The determinants for share repurchase timing and amounts were expanded in 2024 to explicitly include 'the evolution of current and future regulatory capital requirements.' This is a material change from the 2023 disclosure, which listed only 'capital position' and 'deployment opportunities' as primary determinants, suggesting heightened emphasis on regulatory capital planning as a constraint on capital returns.

key_findings.title: Increase in Market Risk VaR Exceptions
key_findings.analysis: The firm reported an increase in Value-at-Risk (VaR) backtesting exceptions from one occasion in 2023 to two occasions in 2024. While the VaR multiplier remained unchanged, this increase represents a deterioration in observed risk performance relative to the prior period, potentially impacting regulatory scrutiny despite no immediate change in capital requirements.

key_findings.title: Reclassification of Fund Relations to Revenue Focus
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure regarding nonconsolidated investment funds shifted from a technical accounting focus in 2023 (under 'Significant Accounting Policies > Consolidation' detailing NAV measurement and consolidation criteria) to a commercial focus in 2024 (under 'Transactions with Affiliated Funds' highlighting management, advisory, and incentive fee revenue). This repositioning emphasizes the economic substance and revenue generation of these relationships over their accounting treatment.

key_findings.title: Fee Waivers No Longer Material
key_findings.analysis: The firm changed its disclosure stance on voluntary financial support to affiliated funds, stating that the impact of fee waivers and deferrals was 'not material' for 2024 and 2023. This contrasts with the 2023 disclosure, which explicitly quantified $33 million in waived fees for 2023 and $595 million for 2021, marking a shift from disclosing specific material impacts to classifying recent support as immaterial.

key_findings.title: Resolution of 2022 Tax Year Issues
key_findings.analysis: The status of the firm's tax issues under the IRS Compliance Assurance Process (CAP) program evolved significantly: the 2022 tax year moved from 'post-filing review' in 2023 to 'resolved pending administrative completion' in 2024. Additionally, the 2023 tax year became subject to post-filing review in 2024, and the CAP program enrollment was extended to include 2025.

key_findings.title: Reduction in Legal Liability Exposure
key_findings.analysis: Management's estimate of the upper end of the range of reasonably possible aggregate loss for legal matters decreased from $2.1 billion in 2023 to $1.7 billion in 2024. This $400 million reduction indicates a material change in the company's disclosed downside legal risk and potential financial exposure.

key_findings.title: Expansion of Litigation Liability Scope in Archegos Case
key_findings.analysis: In 2024, the Appellate Division affirmed the reversal of the dismissal of claims against non-trading underwriters in the ViacomCBS securities class action. This materially expands the roster of liable parties compared to 2023, where only trading underwriters (including GS&Co.) were confirmed to face claims. This change alters the firm's risk landscape by exposing it to broader litigation potential from this matter.

key_findings.title: Material Bankruptcy Event in Vroom Underwriting Litigation
key_findings.analysis: Vroom filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in November 2024, a significant development absent in the 2023 disclosure. This event introduces substantial uncertainty regarding the solvency of the primary issuer and the practical resolution of the securities class action, materially altering the risk profile of GS&Co.'s exposure in this litigation.

key_findings.title: Escalation of Zymergen Litigation via Second Amended Complaint
key_findings.analysis: Plaintiffs filed a second amended complaint in March 2024 regarding the Zymergen IPO litigation, following Zymergen's 2023 bankruptcy. This procedural update extends the litigation timeline and potentially broadens allegations, representing a meaningful escalation of legal risk compared to the 2023 status which only noted the initial bankruptcy and class certification.

key_findings.title: New Material Exposure from Coupang IPO Litigation
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure introduces a new securities class action related to Coupang's $4.6 billion 2021 IPO, with defendants moving to dismiss in July 2023. This represents a new material legal risk addition not present in the 2023 disclosures, expanding the firm's underwriting litigation portfolio.

key_findings.title: Broadening of Executive Compensation Incentive Scope
key_findings.analysis: The investment management services override program participant pool expanded from approximately 800 to 900 employees in 2024, with explicit inclusion of executive officers. This represents a material change in human capital compensation strategy, increasing the breadth of incentive alignment and potential governance oversight requirements.

key_findings.title: Removal of FINRA Liquidity Risk Regulatory Disclosure
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure detailed a June 2023 FINRA proposal requiring liquidity standards and stress testing for broker-dealers. Its complete absence in 2024 suggests either the proposal's withdrawal, adoption with minor changes, or a strategic de-emphasis. This removal reduces transparency on specific operational liquidity risk frameworks, warranting attention.

key_findings.title: Divergence in Risk Governance Disclosure Structure
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure explicitly delineated credit risk management responsibilities between Credit Risk and Market Risk functions for derivatives versus bonds/loans. The removal of this specific governance structure in 2024 suggests a change in how the company discloses or manages operational controls, obscuring the clarity of risk function boundaries.

key_findings.title: Withdrawal of Country-Specific Geopolitical Risk Data
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure provided specific quantitative market exposure data for Argentina ($157 million). This country-specific disclosure was removed in 2024, while Ukraine exposure is still disclosed. This suggests either a material reduction in exposure or a shift in geopolitical risk reporting strategy, impacting transparency on sovereign risk concentrations.

key_findings.title: Reduction in Operational Risk Framework Transparency
key_findings.analysis: Specific details regarding the Business Resilience Risk framework, including Business Continuity Programs (BCP) and crisis management testing, were present in 2023 but removed from the matched disclosure in 2024. This loss of specific operational risk framework details reduces transparency regarding the firm's preparedness for operational disruptions.

key_findings.title: Strategic Shift in Competitive Landscape to Include AI
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 risk factors disclosure explicitly adds 'AI technologies' as a competitive threat intensifying the financial services industry, alongside distributed ledger technologies. This reflects a strategic acknowledgment of AI as a distinct competitive force, marking a shift from the 2023 focus which primarily highlighted distributed ledger technologies and cryptocurrencies.

sources.text: In December 2022, the SEC issued four proposals to reform the U.S. equity market structure.

The SEC proposed establishing a broker-dealer best execution standard, which would require broker-dealers to use reasonable diligence to ascertain the best market for a customer order so that the resultant price to the customer is as favorable as possible under prevailing market conditions.
The best execution standard applies to all securities and supplements, but does not replace, the existing FINRA and Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) best execution rules.

The SEC also proposed, among other things, to require that individual investor orders routed through broker-dealers be exposed to order-by-order competition in qualified auctions; to update the minimum pricing increments, with variable price increments based on the trading characteristics of stocks; and to revise and expand reporting and disclosure requirements relating to execution quality.
The SEC has proposed four rules to reform the U.S. equity market structure, two of which have been adopted.
In 2024, the SEC adopted a rule, effective December 2025, to revise and expand reporting and disclosure requirements relating to execution quality.
In 2024, the SEC also adopted a rule to update the minimum pricing increments, with variable price increments based on the trading characteristics of stocks.
In December 2024, the SEC stayed the implementation of this rule, which would apply starting in November 2025, pending the outcome of litigation challenging the rule.

Limiting the size of our market-making positions can adversely affect our profitability.
In periods when volatility is increasing, but asset values are declining significantly, it may not be possible to sell assets at all or it may only be possible to do so at steep discounts.
